title: Orbit-Adaptive Zero-Shot Forecasting on Spatio-Temporal Graph

problem.claim: Spatio-temporal graph forecasting must transfer knowledge to target domains with scarce or unavailable temporal observations.

gap.claim: Existing node-adaptive spatio-temporal graph neural networks are ineffective in the strict zero-shot setting because their node-specific parameters cannot be inferred without target data.

contributions.claim: The work proposes an Orbit-Adaptive Graph Neural Network framework for zero-shot spatio-temporal graph learning.
The framework characterizes structural roles using automorphism orbits, which represent symmetric positions in a graph.
The framework shares adaptation mechanisms across nodes in the same orbit to learn domain-invariant, structure-aware representations for prediction on unseen graphs.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report extensive experiments across six datasets covering traffic, air quality, and pandemic domains.
The authors report that the proposed framework outperforms existing transfer and naive zero-shot baselines.

narrative_sequence.summary: Forecasting in spatio-temporal graphs faces severe target-domain data scarcity.
The work studies zero-shot learning where only target graph topology is available and no target temporal observations exist.
Node-adaptive methods fail because target-data-dependent node-specific parameters cannot be inferred.
The proposed framework uses automorphism orbits and shared adaptation mechanisms to produce structure-aware representations for unseen graphs.
Experiments on six datasets are reported to outperform transfer and naive zero-shot baselines.

source_observation.claim: Nodes with the same structural role, represented by automorphism orbits, share adaptation mechanisms.

interpretation.claim: Structural equivalence can provide a basis for sharing adaptation when target-domain observations are unavailable.

application.claim: For zero-shot graph prediction, consider grouping entities by structural symmetry or role before designing transferable representations.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether orbit-based sharing is effective for graphs lacking useful symmetries or for domains outside those evaluated.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, model architecture details, training procedure, or quantitative performance margins.
The abstract does not describe computational cost, limitations, or behavior under target graphs with different structural properties.
